content.title: About
content.content: French toast consists of bread slices dipped in a mixture of eggs, milk, and spices, then fried until golden. The “plain” version contains no added toppings such as fruit, syrup, or butter.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish originated in France in the 17th century and was originally called “pain perdu” – “lost bread”.
It was traditionally used to revive stale bread, turning it into a tasty, nutritious meal.
Dense breads like baguette or thick-sliced sandwich bread work best for the recipe.
In the United States French toast is often served with maple syrup, but the plain version is considered healthier.
There are many variations: with cinnamon, vanilla, or even savory cheese versions.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Eggs provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair and maintenance.

items.title: Contains calcium
items.content: Milk contributes calcium, important for bone and tooth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and milk are rich in B2, B6, and B12, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: The combination of carbohydrates from bread and fats from eggs offers a quick energy boost.

items.title: Low added sugar
items.content: A plain preparation contains no added sugars, fitting moderate sugar intake guidelines.

items.title: Egg or dairy allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to eggs or lactose may experience reactions.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Using a lot of butter or oil for frying can make the dish calorie‑rich.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If salt is added, total sodium intake should be monitored.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Traditional bread contains gluten, making it unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve French toast hot; you may sprinkle cinnamon, add fresh berries, nuts, or a drizzle of honey if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Best enjoyed fresh. Leftovers can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days and reheated in a skillet or microwave.
